clue.text: Father's foil a trick for lover

parts.note: a flam is an old word for a sham or deceptive trick
a beau is a boyfriend or admirer

explanation.surface: A fencing father sets a trap for his daughter's suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father's foil' looks like a fencing sword, but it is G. K. Chesterton's Father Brown, whose recurring adversary and later friend is the thief Flambeau.
explanation.definitionFit: In Chesterton's detective stories the master thief is the priest-detective's chief opponent and partner, his literary foil.

clue.text: Lord's notice sen on the Great North Road

definitions.note: the definition reads as Lord is, the 's being a link

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
the A1 is Britain's Great North Road, London to Edinburgh, written with the figure 1 as letter I

explanation.surface: A peer's sign is spotted beside Britain's main road north.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as published reads 'sen', evidently a slip for 'seen', a link word. The A1 is Britain's historic Great North Road.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hebrew title used for God in the Old Testament, meaning my Lord.

clue.text: Currently opposed to preparation of tempuras

indicators.note: preparing food means working it up, so the letters of the dish are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone objects to how Japanese battered food is being cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Going against the current of a river is moving in the opposite direction to the flow.

clue.text: Playwright's letter to the Greek Fiddler

definitions.note: the definition reads as playwright is, the 's being a link

parts.note: pi is a letter of the alphabet as the Greeks know it
the emperor Nero is said to have fiddled while Rome burned

explanation.surface: A dramatist writes a note to a Greek violinist.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Arthur Wing Pinero was an English dramatist, author of The Magistrate and Trelawny of the Wells.

clue.text: Deceive lord taking dip in Scottish river

indicators.note: the lord goes for a swim, so his word is placed inside the river's

parts.note: the Dee flows through Aberdeenshire to the sea at Aberdeen
lud is the form in 'm'lud', how a judge is addressed

explanation.surface: A nobleman bathing in a Highland river tricks someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To delude someone is to mislead or fool them into false belief, a close synonym.

clue.text: For pretty woman, surgeon's work reduced lump

parts.note: a doll is an attractive young woman, in dated slang

indicators.note: the word for the surgeon's task is cut short to its opening pair of letters

parts.note: an operation is what a surgeon performs

explanation.surface: A cosmetic surgeon cuts down a lump to make a woman pretty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' shortens OPERATION to OP, the usual abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollop is a shapeless blob or mass, especially of soft food, so a lump.

clue.text: Pick Enigmatist and his mum together — they're the best …

parts.note: to opt is to choose or pick
the setter of the puzzle refers to himself, so I
ma is a mother

explanation.surface: Choose the setter and his mother as the finest pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Optima is the plural of optimum, the best or most favourable conditions or results.

clue.text: Disinclined to some poetry

parts.note: a, as in a quantity of something
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Someone is reluctant to read any poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse to something means being unwilling or opposed to it, a synonym.

clue.text: Protest to husband about parent's last place of rest

indicators.note: the protest wraps around the final letter of parent

parts.note: a sit-in is a protest occupation

indicators.note: only the final letter of parent is taken

parts.note: a groom is a newly married husband

explanation.surface: A man stages a demonstration over where his late father was buried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last place of rest' reads like a grave; 'last' belongs to the wordplay, leaving 'place of rest'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounge or living room is where people relax, so a place to rest.

clue.text: … his dad sold many clothes

indicators.note: the phrase clothes the answer, wrapping it inside its letters

explanation.surface: The setter's father was a prolific clothing seller.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues 6, so 'his' is the setter's. 'clothes' looks like goods sold, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Old man is informal for a father, so the setter's dad.

clue.text: Question about Lord Owen, perhaps unusual hero: he doeth resuscitation!

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement of letters signals that they are reordered

explanation.surface: An odd hero who revives the dying is wanted, asks someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Owen is David Owen, the former Labour Foreign Secretary, who trained as a medical doctor, so he is the kind of person this call seeks.
explanation.definitionFit: The call made in a theatre or plane when someone falls ill seeks a medic such as the physician-politician David Owen.

parts.note: the reference points to the phrase at 12, meaning indoors within one's own dwelling

explanation.definitionFit: Being at one's residence means being inside one's house, a straight synonym.

clue.text: See 10
See 21
A dedicated angler may take a chance

definitions.meaning: a keen fisherman throws out his line again and again, so many times
drawing tokens at random to decide something is leaving it to luck

explanation.definitionFit: Drawing straws or tokens to settle a matter is leaving the outcome to chance.

clue.text: One can't hold the binoculars still!

definitions.text: One can't hold the binoculars still!

parts.words: One can't hold the binoculars still!
parts.note: reads as a nervous, jerky person, but means a keen birdwatcher who chases rare sightings

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a dedicated birdwatcher who travels to see rare species, always reaching for binoculars.

clue.text: Strap contains resistance of crowd

indicators.note: the strap holds the letter inside it

parts.note: a thong is a narrow leather strap
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A leather strap holds back a resisting mob.
explanation.definitionFit: A throng is a large densely packed crowd of people, a synonym.

clue.text: 23's object turns out to be a flower

indicators.note: the letters turn out differently, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: 23 is DOCTOR; MO, Medical Officer, is a doctor, plus the S of the possessive
an aim is an object or goal

explanation.surface: The physician's real aim proves to be a blossom.
explanation.walkthrough: MO'S AIM, the doctor's object, is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimosa is a plant with fluffy yellow flowers, sold as a cut flower.

clue.text: Prominent pair left 12: they won't want to draw one

definitions.text: they won't want to draw one

parts.note: Clare Short and Jack Straw, two leading Labour figures, on the left in the House of Commons
Clare Short and Jack Straw, two leading Labour figures, on the left in the House of Commons

explanation.surface: Two well-known left-wing MPs in Parliament dread a losing draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is the Labour Party, and 12 is IN THE HOUSE, the Commons, where Short and Straw sat.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever draws the shortest stalk in a lottery gets the unpleasant job, so nobody wants it.

clue.text: What do I use for distillation? This must be the answer!

definitions.text: What do I use for distillation?
definitions.meaning: a glass vessel with a long bent neck used by chemists to distil liquids
a quick, sharp or witty reply

explanation.definitionFit: A retort is both a laboratory distilling flask and a sharp rejoinder.

clue.text: Women with identification receive gizmo

parts.note: to get is to receive

explanation.surface: Women showing ID are handed a gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A widget is a small gadget or device, a casual synonym for gizmo.

clue.text: Right behind him 12 — 22 may or may not be!

definitions.text: Right behind him 12 — 22 may or may not be!

parts.words: Right behind him 12 — 22 may or may not be!
parts.note: the Tory right in the House of Commons backed this leader; his rival Portillo, at 22, perhaps not

explanation.definitionFit: He was elected Conservative leader in 2001, beating Kenneth Clarke after Portillo was eliminated, backed by the party's right wing.

clue.text: I will shortly get round supporting left and I'm 12

definitions.note: the definition says I am in the house, an MP

indicators.note: in an across answer the later pieces come after the one they support

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
the contraction of I will is I'll
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone promises to come round and back the left, speaking as a member of the House.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is IN THE HOUSE; Michael Portillo was a Conservative MP and leadership contender in 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Portillo sat in the House of Commons as a Tory MP, so he can say he is in the House.

clue.text: See 10
In attendance, your turn

indicators.note: the abbreviation for your sits inside the word for attendance

parts.note: the gate is the attendance at a sports match

explanation.surface: Someone at an event is told it is their go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In attendance' reads as present; it is 'In' signalling insertion plus 'attendance', the crowd at a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to turn or revolve, spinning about a centre.

clue.text: Some species producing a green variety

indicators.note: a variety of the letters, signalling that they are reordered

explanation.surface: Breeding a new kind of green plant creates several species.
explanation.definitionFit: Genera are taxonomic groups each containing a number of related species.
